dedupe_keys.name: riscad relational chemical accident database aist japan

description: A Japanese database of chemical accidents run by AIST. The RISCAD page says it builds on AIST's collections of accident cases involving explosives and high-pressure gas under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, hazardous materials under the Fire Service Act and other chemical plant accidents; each accident is organised as a time series of events, analysed with AIST's accident analysis method PFA into accident progression flow diagrams, and linked to hazard information on the chemicals and to process flows. As of 26 October 2017 it held 7,106 cases from 28 October 1949 onwards, 6,194 in Japan, 1,402 fatal and 107 with progression flow diagrams, with weekly chemical accident news. The page says RISCAD is currently under maintenance and unavailable, with reopening to be announced on AIST's site; access terms and licence are not stated on the page read. Coverage is mainly Japan, with some overseas cases. Caveats: offline at the time of reading, and counts date from 2017. For simulation it gives long accident histories with event sequences for chemical plant cascading failure models. Related catalogue records include ZEMA and eMARS.
